To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the most frequently occurring wind directions appear to be responsible for dune formation and the strongest winds for dune orientation; and (2) topography plays an important role in shaping wind trajectories.

1) the most frequent wind direction is responsible for sediment supply to dunes, while the strongest wind drives dune orientation; 2) topography influences wind orientation; and 3) back-trajectories incorporating dust transport and potential deposition suggest both westerlies and northerlies deliver fine-grained material, and that the source areas lie in a region of mixed sediment grain sizes.

the orientation of dunes and the direction of wind trajectories are strongly influenced by the topography of the Ili Basin, and that the location of loess sites is determined by both the direction and strength of winds, as well as the source area.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aeolian landforms and sediment fluxes in the Ili Basin are strongly linked to the region's topography and the complex interactions between wind regimes, sediment supply and topography.

1) the distribution of linear dune orientations is strongly influenced by topographic features, 2) dune orientation is influenced by both the direction of the sand-shifting winds and the strength of the wind regime, 3) dune morphology is strongly related to the direction of the prevailing winds, and 4) the location of dune fields is strongly linked to the location of source areas for fine-grained sediment.

the timing and magnitude of aeolian activity in Central Asia are highly variable; dune orientations are influenced by topography; dunes are likely to be the product of multiple wind events and are not a simple reflection of the wind regime; and the loess deposits of the Tien Shan are likely to have been derived from a variety of source regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relationship between aeolain flux and deposition is more complex than is currently appreciated, and that the aeolian landforms of Central Asia are sensitive indicators of the interactions between wind regimes, local topography and sediment availability.
aeolian landforms can provide a powerful proxy for wind regimes in the Central Asian steppe, and that their distribution and morphology are strongly influenced by the topography.
the distribution of aeolian landforms is not a straightforward reflection of wind regimes.
